decisions.question: What urgency values are allowed, and are they distinct from Ticket.Priority?
decisions.answer: Reuse the existing Ticket.Priority allowed values for urgency:  - Critical - High - Medium - Low  However, SuggestedUrgency and ReviewedUrgency must remain separate fields from the authoritative Ticket.Priority. Sharing the same allowed-value set does not imply that urgency and priority are the same business attribute. No automatic or implicit mapping to Ticket.Priority is permitted.

decisions.question: Which roles may review, accept, or override urgency and over which tickets?
decisions.answer: The following existing roles may review, accept, or override AI-suggested urgency:  1. Support Agent: Only tickets currently assigned to that Agent, subject to valid current tenant, primary-team, and ticket authorization. 2. Support Manager: All tickets belonging to their currently assigned teams, including team-assigned tickets without an individual Agent. 3. Tenant Admin: Any ticket within their own tenant. 4. Platform Admin: No individual tenant-ticket urgency review or access.  Revalidate current role, tenant, team, ticket, and assignment authorization on every review or override action. Do not introduce any new role, permission-grant mechanism, or exception.

decisions.question: Does human review update authoritative Ticket.Priority?
decisions.answer: ReviewedUrgency must remain separate review metadata and must not update the authoritative Ticket.Priority.  - On acceptance, set ReviewedUrgency equal to SuggestedUrgency. - On override, set ReviewedUrgency to the selected valid urgency value. - Preserve SuggestedUrgency unchanged in both cases. - Record ReviewedBy and ReviewedAt for every completed review. - Do not modify Ticket.Priority through the urgency review workflow, regardless of the reviewer's role.  If an authoritative Ticket.Priority change is required, it must use the existing separate Category/Priority change workflow under FR-TM-14, including its role, tenant, team, ticket-state, validation, activity-history, and audit requirements.  An urgency review must never bypass existing ticket permissions or state restrictions.
